closure.FU4: OPEN, left as needs-design; leaving it is safe. The fixer’s reasoning holds: with /iu the look-behind blocks after any letter, so é(c) 2026, Café(r), Société(c) 2026 and 日本(c)2026 stop converting (probe of a +u copy). But the present byte reading is not a behaviour worth keeping for its own sake: ü(c) 2026 is already left (ü ends in byte 0xBC, which Latin-1 reads as ¼) while é(c) 2026 converts, and (c)(ü) is left while (c)(é) and (c)(ñ) convert. All of it is stable across passes, pre-dates the delta for the look-behind, and loses nothing. The contained doc option from the gate (“an ASCII letter or digit”) was not taken, so README.md:376 still says “letters or digits”. Dan’s call between /iu (one consistent rule, with é(c) 2026 then left as typed like Acme(r)) and the doc wording.
